segments.en: Muse, tell me the deeds of golden Aphrodite the Cyprian, who stirs up sweet passion in the gods and subdues the tribes of mortal men and birds that fly in air and all the many creatures that the dry land rears, and all that the sea: all these love the deeds of rich-crowned Cytherea. Yet there are three hearts that she cannot bend nor yet ensnare. First is the daughter of Zeus who holds the aegis, bright-eyed Athena; for she has no pleasure in the deeds of golden Aphrodite, but delights in wars and in the work of Ares, in strifes and battles and in preparing famous crafts. She first taught earthly craftsmen to make chariots of war and cars variously wrought with bronze, and she, too, teaches tender maidens in the house and puts knowledge of goodly arts in each one's mind. Nor does laughter-loving Aphrodite ever tame in love Artemis, the huntress with shafts of gold; for she loves archery and the slaying of wild beasts in the mountains, the lyre also and dancing and thrilling cries
segments.zh:
繆斯啊，請說出金色的阿芙羅狄忒的事蹟吧，她是塞浦路斯的女神，
在諸神心中喚起甜蜜的欲望，制服了凡人的各族、
在空中飛翔的鳥類，以及乾地所養育的眾多生靈，
還有海洋中的一切；這一切都鍾愛富冠的庫忒拉的女神的事蹟。
然而有三顆心是她無法彎折，也無法困住的。
首先是持盾牌之宙斯的女兒，明眸的雅典娜；
因為她不喜歡金色的阿芙羅狄忒的事蹟，反倒喜歡戰爭和阿瑞斯的工作，
喜歡紛爭與戰鬥，以及準備名聲遠播的手藝。
她首先教授地上的工匠製造戰車
和用銅製作的各式裝飾戰車，她也教導房中的柔弱女郎，
將美好的藝術知識放入各人的心智。
愛笑的阿芙羅狄忒也從未能用愛馴服金箭的狩獵女神阿爾忒彌斯；
因為她熱愛射箭和在山中獵殺野獸，
也熱愛七弦琴、舞蹈和尖銳的呼喊

segments.en: and shady woods and the cities of upright men. Nor yet does the pure maiden Hestia love Aphrodite's works. She was the first-born child of wily Cronos and youngest too,Cronos swallowed each of his children the moment that they were born, but ultimately was forced to disgorge them. Hestia, being the first to be swallowed, was the last to be disgorged, and so was at once the first and latest born of the children of Cronos. Cp. Hesiod Theogony, ll. 495-7. by will of Zeus who holds the aegis, —a queenly maid whom both Poseidon and Apollo sought to wed. But she was wholly unwilling, nay, stubbornly refused; and touching the head of father Zeus who holds the aegis, she, that fair goddess, swear a great oath which has in truth been fulfilled, that she would be a maiden all her days. So Zeus the Father gave her an high honor instead of marriage, and she has her place in the midst of the house and has the richest portion. In all the temples of the gods she has a share of honor, and among all mortal men she is chief of the goddesses. Of these three Aphrodite cannot bend or ensnare the hearts. But of all others there is nothing among the blessed gods or among mortal men that has escaped Aphrodite. Even the heart of Zeus, who delights in thunder, is led astray by her; though he is greatest of all and has the lot of highest majesty, she beguiles even his wise heart whensoever she pleases, and mates him with mortal women,

和陰影的林地以及直心人類的城邑。純潔的少女赫斯提亞也不喜歡阿芙羅狄忒的事蹟。
她是狡詐的克洛諾斯的長子，同時又是最幼的，
（克洛諾斯在每個孩兒降生之時即吞下之，後來終被迫吐出。赫斯提亞先被吞下，故最後被吐出，因而既是克洛諾斯的最長也是最幼之女。參《赫西俄德神統》495-497行。）
以持盾牌之宙斯的意志，是一位皇后般的少女，波塞頓和阿波羅都曾求娶她。
但她完全不願意，反倒頑強地拒絕；她觸及父親持盾牌之宙斯的頭，
這位美麗的女神起了一個偉大的誓，業已真實應驗，
她將終身保持少女之身。因此父親宙斯給了她高的榮譽來代替婚姻，
她居住在家的中央，擁有最豐裕的份額。
在諸神的所有廟宇中她都分享榮譽，在所有的凡人中她是女神中的首要者。
這三位中阿芙羅狄忒無法彎折或困住她們的心。
但在其他所有者中，在蒙福的諸神或凡人間，沒有任何人逃脫了阿芙羅狄忒。
即使愛好雷電的宙斯的心也被她所引導；雖然他最為偉大，擁有最高尊貴的命運，
她欺瞞了他的智慧，使他與凡人女子結合，

ἐς Πάφον· ἔνθα δέ οἱ τέμενος βωμός τε θυώδης.
segments.en: unknown to Hera, his sister and his wife, the grandest far in beauty among the deathless goddesses —most glorious is she whom wily Cronos with her mother Rhea did beget: and Zeus, whose wisdom is everlasting, made her his chaste and careful wife. But upon Aphrodite herself Zeus cast sweet desire to be joined in love with a mortal man, to the end that, very soon, not even she should be innocent of a mortal's love; lest laughter-loving Aphrodite should one day softly smile and say mockingly among all the gods that she had joined the gods in love with mortal women who bare sons of death to the deathless gods, and had mated the goddesses with mortal men. And so he put in her heart sweet desire for Anchises who at that time among the steep hills of many-fountained Ida was tending cattle, and in shape was like the immortal gods. Therefore, when laughter-loving Aphrodite saw him, she loved him, and terribly desire seized her in her heart. She went to Cyprus, to Paphos, where her precinct is and fragrant altar, and passed into her sweet-smelling temple.
segments.zh:
隱瞞於赫拉，他的妹妹和妻子，在眾不死的女神中美貌最為偉大——
狡詐的克洛諾斯與她的母親瑞亞所生者最為光榮；而宙斯，其智慧永恆不變，
使她成為他貞潔與謹慎的妻子。但宙斯對阿芙羅狄忒自己投下了甜蜜的欲望，
令她與凡人結合，目的是為了很快地，連她也不應免於凡人之愛；
免得愛笑的阿芙羅狄忒有朝一日溫柔地微笑，在所有諸神中嘲笑般地說，
她曾使諸神與凡人女子結合，那些女子為不死的諸神生了死亡之子，
使女神與凡人男子結合。因此他在她心中放入甜蜜的欲望，
渴望與那時在多泉之伊達的陡峭山巒中牧牛的安喀塞斯結合，
他的形貌如同不死的諸神。因此當愛笑的阿芙羅狄忒看見他時，她愛上了他，
可怕的欲望抓住了她的心。她前往塞浦路斯，前往帕福斯，
那裡有她的聖地與芬芳的祭壇，進入了她香氣芬芳的廟宇。

segments.en: There she went in and put to the glittering doors, and there the Graces bathed her with heavenly oil such as blooms upon the bodies of the eternal gods —oil divinely sweet, which she had by her, filled with fragrance. And laughter-loving Aphrodite put on all her rich clothes, and when she had decked herself with gold, she left sweet-smelling Cyprus and went in haste towards Troy, swiftly travelling high up among the clouds. So she came to many-fountained Ida, the mother of wild creatures and went straight to the homestead across the mountains. After her came grey wolves, fawning on her, and grim-eyed lions, and bears, and fleet leopards, ravenous for deer: and she was glad in heart to see them, and put desire in their breasts, so that they all mated, two together, about the shadowy coombes. But she herself came to the neat-built shelters, and him she found left quite alone in the homestead —the hero Anchises who was comely as the gods. All the others were following the herds over the grassy pastures, and he, left quite alone in the homestead,
segments.zh: 她進去關上了閃耀的門扉，那裡眾恩典女神用天國的油為她沐浴，那油開綻在永恆諸神的身軀之上——神聖而芬芳的油，她身邊備著，充滿香氣。愛笑的阿芙羅狄忒穿上了她所有華美的衣裳，當她用黃金飾裝自己後，她離開了芬香的塞浦路斯，匆匆趕向特洛伊，在雲層之上迅疾地高飛。於是她來到泉水眾多的伊達山，野獸之母，直行穿過群山抵達牧場。灰色的狼群跟隨她，搖尾乞憐，兇眼的獅子、熊和奔捷的豹子也跟隨，飢渴於鹿肉；她見到它們心中喜悅，在它們胸中放入慾望，使得它們全都成對交配，在幽暗的山谷裡。但她自己來到精心築造的棚舍，她發現他獨自留在牧場中——美如諸神的英雄安喀塞斯。其他人都跟隨羊群在長草的牧地上，而他獨自留在牧場中，

segments.en: was roaming hither and thither and playing thrillingly upon the lyre. And Aphrodite, the daughter of Zeus stood before him, being like a pure maiden in height and mien, that he should not be frightened when he took heed of her with his eyes. Now when Anchises saw her, he marked her well and wondered at her mien and height and shining garments. For she was clad in a robe out-shining the brightness of fire, a splendid robe of gold, enriched with all manner of needlework, which shimmered like the moon over her tender breasts, a marvel to see. Also she wore twisted brooches and shining earrings in the form of flowers;
segments.zh: 四處漫遊並在七弦琴上悅耳地彈奏。宙斯之女阿芙羅狄忒站在他面前，身形和儀態宛如純潔的少女，使他看到她時不會驚恐。當安喀塞斯看到她時，他仔細觀察她，驚歎於她的儀態、身形和閃耀的衣衫。她穿著一襲超越火光亮度的長衫，華麗的黃金長衫，飾以各式精細的刺繡，閃爍如月光灑在她柔嫩的胸膛，令人嘆為觀止。她還戴著扭轉的胸針和形似花朵的耀眼耳環；

segments.en: and round her soft throat were lovely necklaces. And Anchises was seized with love, and said to her: “Hail, lady, whoever of the blessed ones you are that are come to this house, whether Artemis, or Leto, or golden Aphrodite, or high-born Themis, or bright-eyed Athena. Or, maybe, you are one of the Graces come hither, who bear the gods company and are called immortal, or else one of the Nymphs who haunt the pleasant woods, or of those who inhabit this lovely mountain and the springs of rivers and grassy meads.
segments.zh: 她柔软的喉間圍繞著可愛的項鍊。安喀塞斯被愛所攫獲，向她說道：「安康，夫人，你是諸福者之一誰呢，來到此屋——是阿爾忒彌斯，或是勒托，或是黃金的阿芙羅狄忒，或是高貴的忒彌斯，或是明眼的雅典娜。或者，你也許是眾恩典之一前來此地，她們與諸神相伴並被稱為不朽者，或者是居於悅人的林木之中的仙女之一，或是那住在這美麗山嶺的，或是河流泉源和長草草地的。

segments.en: I will make you an altar upon a high peak in a far seen place, and will sacrifice rich offerings to you at all seasons. And do you feel kindly towards me and grant that I may become a man very eminent among the Trojans, and give me strong offspring for the time to come. As for my own self, let me live long and happily, seeing the light of the sun, and come to the threshold of old age, a man prosperous among the people.” Thereupon Aphrodite the daughter of Zeus answered him: “Anchises, most glorious of all men born on earth, know that I am no goddess: why do you liken me to the deathless ones? Nay, I am but a mortal, and a woman was the mother that bare me. Otreus of famous name is my father, if so be you have heard of him, and he reigns over all Phrygia rich in fortresses. But I know your speech well beside my own, for a Trojan nurse brought me up at home: she took me from my dear mother and reared me thenceforth when I was a little child. So comes it, then, that I well know your tongue also. And now the Slayer of Argus with the golden wand has caught me up from the dance of huntress Artemis, her with the golden arrows. segments.en: playing together; and an innumerable company encircled us: from these the Slayer of Argus with the golden wand rapt me away. He carried me over many fields of mortal men and over much land untilled and unpossessed, where savage wild-beasts roam through shady coombes, until I thought never again to touch the life-giving earth with my feet. And he said that I should be called the wedded wife of Anchises, and should bear you goodly children. But when he had told and advised me, he, the strong Slayer of Argos, went back to the families of the deathless gods, while I am now come to you: for unbending necessity is upon me. But I beseech you by Zeus and by your noble parents —for no base folk could get such a son as you —take me now, stainless and unproved in love, and show me to your father and careful mother and to your brothers sprung from the same stock. I shall be no ill-liking daughter for them, but a likely. Moreover, send a messenger quickly to the swift-horsed Phrygians, to tell my father and my sorrowing mother; and they will send you gold in plenty and woven stuffs, many splendid gifts;

他說我應該被稱為安喀塞斯的新娶妻子，

強大的殺死阿爾戈斯的神靈就回到了不朽的眾神之中，

因為無法違背的必然壓在我身上。
然而我以宙斯起誓求告你，

我將不是他們討厭的女兒，而是令人喜愛的。

And when they had gone up upon the well-fitted bed, first Anchises took off her bright jewelry of pins and twisted brooches and earrings and necklaces, and loosed her girdle and stripped off her bright garments and laid them down upon a silver-studded seat. Then by the will of the gods and destiny he lay with her, a mortal man with an immortal goddess, not clearly knowing what he did. But at the time when the herdsmen drive their oxen and hardy sheep back to the fold from the flowery pastures, even then Aphrodite poured soft sleep upon Anchises, but herself put on her rich raiment. And when the bright goddess had fully clothed herself, she stood by the couch, and her head reached to the well-hewn roof-tree; from her cheeks shone unearthly beauty such as belongs to rich-crowned Cytherea. Then she aroused him from sleep and opened her mouth and said:“Up, son of Dardanus! —why sleep you so heavily? —and consider whether I look as I did when first you saw me with your eyes.”
segments.zh: 他自己在高山上殺死的那頭牛。當他們上了鋪陳得很好的床榻，首先安喀伊塞斯脫下她發亮的飾物——別針、扭曲的胸針、耳環和項鍊，解開她的腰帶，剝去她明亮的衣衫，把它們放在飾有銀釘的座位上。接著，遵循諸神和命運的意旨，他與她相交，一個凡人與一位不朽的女神，並未清楚明白自己在做什麼。但正當牧人們把牛群和強健的羊從花卉盛開的牧場趕回羊棧的時候，正是這時阿芙羅狄忒向安喀伊塞斯傾注了柔和的睡眠，而她自己穿上了華貴的衣袍。當明亮的女神完全穿戴好了自己，她站在床榻旁，她的頭觸及設計精妙的屋頑；從她的雙頰放射出非凡的美，那種美屬於戴著豐盛王冠的基塞拉。於是她喚醒了他的睡眠，張開她的嘴說：「起來，達達諾斯的兒子！——你何以睡得如此沉重？——並且想想我是否看起來如同你最初用眼睛看到我時的樣子。」

segments.en: So she spake. And he awoke in a moment and obeyed her. But when he saw the neck and lovely eyes of Aphrodite, he was afraid and turned his eyes aside another way, hiding his comely face with his cloak. Then he uttered winged words and entreated her: “So soon as ever I saw you with my eyes, goddess, I knew that you were divine; but you did not tell me truly. Yet by Zeus who holds the aegis I beseech you, leave me not to lead a palsied life among men, but have pity on me; for he who lies with a deathless goddess is no hale man afterwards.”Then Aphrodite the daughter of Zeus answered him: “Anchises, most glorious of mortal men, take courage and be not too fearful in your heart. You need fear no harm from me nor from the other blessed ones, for you are dear to the gods: and you shall have a dear son who shall reign among the Trojans, and children's children after him, springing up continually. His name shall be Aeneas,The name Aeneas is here connected with the epithet ainos (awful): similarly the name Odysseus is derived (in Od. i. 62) from ὀδυσσομαι (I grieve). because I felt awful grief in that I laid me in the bed of a mortal man:
segments.zh: 她這樣說。他立刻醒來並服從了她。但當他看到阿芙羅狄忒的頸項和可愛的眼睛，他感到害怕並把眼睛轉向別處，用斗篷遮蔽了他美麗的面容。於是他說出了帶翼的言辭並懇求她：「我一用眼睛看到你，女神啊，我就知道你是神聖的；但你沒有真實地告訴我。然而以持盾牌的宙斯的名義我懇求你，不要讓我在人間過著癱瘓的生活，而是對我有憐憫之心；因為誰與一位不朽的女神相交，誰以後就不是一個健康的人。」於是宙斯的女兒阿芙羅狄忒回答他：「安喀伊塞斯啊，最光榮的凡人，要有勇氣，不要在你的心中過於害怕。你不需要害怕來自我或其他有福者的傷害，因為你對諸神是親愛的；你將有一位親愛的兒子，他將統治特洛伊人，他之後還有孩子的孩子，繼續湧現。他的名字將是埃涅阿斯，因為我在與一個凡人躺在同一床榻上時感到了可怕的悲痛；

Ζηνὸς ἐφημοσύνῃσι διάκτορος Ἀργειφόντης,

segments.en: yet are those of your race always the most like to gods of all mortal men in beauty and in stature.Aphrodite extenuates her disgrace by claiming that the race of Anchises is almost divine, as is shown in the persons of Ganymedes and Tithonus. Verily wise Zeus carried off golden-haired Ganymedes because of his beauty, to be amongst the Deathless Ones and pour drink for the gods in the house of Zeus — a wonder to see—,honored by all the immortals as he draws the red nectar from the golden bowl. But grief that could not be soothed filled the heart of Tros; for he knew not whither the heaven-sent whirlwind had caught up his dear son, so that he mourned him always, unceasingly, until Zeus pitied him and gave him high-stepping horses such as carry the immortals as recompense for his son. These he gave him as a gift. And at the command of Zeus, the Guide, the slayer of Argus, told him all, and how his son would be deathless and unageing, even as the gods. So when Tros heard these tidings from Zeus, he no longer kept mourning but rejoiced in his heart and rode joyfully with his storm-footed horses.So also golden-throned Eos rapt away Tithonus who was of your race and like the deathless gods.
segments.zh: 然而你的種族之人總是在美和身材上最像諸神的所有凡人。確實聰慧的宙斯因為黃金髮色的伽倪墨得斯的美而將他奪走，使他在永生者之中，在宙斯的殿堂為諸神斟飲——這是一個可看的奇蹟——，當他從金碗中汲出紅色的甘露時受到所有不朽者的尊榮。但無法平撫的悲痛充滿了特洛斯的心；因為他不知道天送的旋風把他親愛的兒子捲向了何處，所以他總是為他哀悼，不斷地哀悼，直到宙斯憐憫了他，並作為補償給了他高步的馬匹，這樣的馬匹運載不朽者。他把它們作為禮物給了他。按照宙斯的命令，引路者、殺死阿爾戈斯的赫爾墨斯告訴了他一切，並告訴他他的兒子將是不朽的和不衰老的，就像諸神一樣。所以當特洛斯聽到了來自宙斯的這些消息，他不再持續哀悼而是在他的心中感到歡喜，並騎著他的暴風足馬高興地馳騁。同樣地金座的厄俄斯奪走了提堤翁，他是你的種族中的人並且像不朽的諸神。

segments.en: And she went to ask the dark-clouded Son of Cronos that he should be deathless and live eternally; and Zeus bowed his head to her prayer and fulfilled her desire. Too simple was queenly Eos: she thought not in her heart to ask youth for him and to strip him of the slough of deadly age. So while he enjoyed the sweet flower of life he lived rapturously with golden-throned Eos, the early-born, by the streams of Ocean, at the ends of the earth; but when the first grey hairs began to ripple from his comely head and noble chin, queenly Eos kept away from his bed, though she cherished him in her house and nourished him with food and ambrosia and gave him rich clothing. But when loathsome old age pressed full upon him, and he could not move nor lift his limbs, this seemed to her in her heart the best counsel: she laid him in a room and put to the shining doors. There he babbles endlessly, and no more has strength at all, such as once he had in his supple limbs. I would not have you be deathless among the deathless gods
segments.zh:
她去祈求烏雲籠罩的克洛諾斯之子
使他永不死去、永遠長生；宙斯低眉應允
她的禱詞、成全了她的所欲。
貴婦厄俄斯實在過於單純：她心中未曾思慮
要為他求得青春、剝去他致命的衰老之軀。
所以他享受著生命的甜美花朵之時，
他與金座的厄俄斯、早生的女神
在俄刻阿諾斯的河畔、在大地的邊際，
狂喜地活著；但當第一道灰髮開始
在他俊美的頭顱和高貴的下巴上泛起漣漪時，
貴婦厄俄斯便遠離他的床榻，
雖然她在家中珍愛他、以食物和神酒餵養他、
給予他華美的衣裳。但當可厭的衰老
完全壓向他、他無法動彈、無法舉起他的四肢時，
這在她心中似乎是最好的謀策：她把他
放在一間房內、關上閃耀的門。
他在那裡喋喋不休地言語、不止，
再也沒有力量，如他柔軟四肢曾有的那般。
我不願你在不死的諸神中永不死去

segments.en: and live continually after such sort. Yet if you could live on such as now you are in look and in form, and be called my husband, sorrow would not then enfold my careful heart. But, as it is, harshSo Christ connecting the word withὠμός. L. and S. give = ὁμοῖος, “common to all.” old age will soon enshroud you — ruthless age which stands someday at the side of every man, deadly, wearying, dreaded even by the gods.And now because of you I shall have great shame among the deathless gods henceforth, continually. For until now they feared my jibes and the wiles by which, or soon or late, I mated all the immortals with mortal women, making them all subject to my will. But now my mouth shall no more have this power among the gods; for very great has been my madness, my miserable and dreadful madness, and I went astray out of my mind who have gotten a child beneath my girdle, mating with a mortal man. As for the child, as soon as he sees the light of the sun, the deep-breasted mountain Nymphs who inhabit this great and holy mountain shall bring him up. They rank neither with mortals nor with immortals:
segments.zh:
並如此不斷地活著。但若你能保持
現在的樣貌和形態、被稱為我的丈夫，
那麼悲痛就不會籠罩我謹慎的心。
但現在不是這樣，嚴酷的衰老很快就要籠罩你——
無情的年紀，它終有一日站在每個人的身側，
致命的、令人疲憊的、連諸神也畏懼的。
因為你的緣故，我今後將在不死的諸神中承受巨大的恥辱，
不斷地。因為到如今他們都害怕我的嘲笑
和我的詭計，藉著這些詭計，遲早我都讓
所有不死者與凡人女子結合，
使他們都服從我的意志。但現在我的嘴在諸神中
將不再有這樣的力量；因為我的瘋狂是多麼巨大，
我的悲慘可怕的瘋狂，我心神蕩漾、迷失理智，
我與一個凡人交合、懷了一個孩子在我腹中。
至於這個孩子，一旦他看見太陽的光芒，
深胸的山地仙女們、住在這個偉大聖潔的山上的仙女們
就會撫養他。她們既不同於凡人也不同於不死者：

segments.en: long indeed do they live, eating heavenly food and treading the lovely dance among the immortals, and with them the Sileni and the sharp-eyed Slayer of Argus mate in the depths of pleasant caves; but at their birth pines or high-topped oaks spring up with them upon the fruitful earth, beautiful, flourishing trees, towering high upon the lofty mountains (and men call them holy places of the immortals, and never mortal lops them with the axe); but when the fate of death is near at hand, first those lovely trees wither where they stand, and the bark shrivels away about them, and the twigs fall down, and at last the life of the Nymph and of the tree leave the light of the sun together. These Nymphs shall keep my son with them and rear him, and as soon as he is come to lovely boyhood, the goddesses will bring him here to you and show you your child. But, that I may tell you all that I have in mind, I will come here again towards the fifth year and bring you my son. So soon as ever you have seen him —a scion to delight the eyes —, you will rejoice in beholding him; for he shall be most godlike:
segments.zh:
她們活得很久，食著天界的食物、在不死者中踏著柔美的舞蹈，
與她們一起、西勒諾斯和銳眼的阿格斯殺手
在愉悅洞穴的深處交合；但她們生下時
松樹或高頂的橡樹與她們一起
在肥沃的地上生出、美麗、興盛的樹木、
聳立在高聳的山嶺之上（人們稱呼它們為
不死者的聖地、凡人絕不用斧頭砍伐它們）；
但當死的命運臨近時，首先那些柔美的樹木
就在原地枯萎、樹皮在它們周圍皺縮、
枝條紛紛落下、最後仙女的生命和樹的生命
一同離開太陽的光芒。這些仙女們將照顧我的兒子、
養育他，一旦他進入柔美的童年時，
女神們就會把他帶到你這裡、給你看你的孩子。
但為了把我心中所有的意思都告訴你，
我會在第五年時再次來到這裡、把我的兒子帶給你。
一旦你看到他——令眼睛喜悅的後代——，
